# Daysift

> Find anything. Instantly.

Daysift is a Chrome browser extension that provides instant search across your browsing history and work applications. It functions as a command palette (similar to Spotlight on Mac, Alfred, or Raycast) but for your browser.

## Problems it solves

- Cannot find a document, page, or tab you were working on recently
- Chrome's built-in history search is slow and limited
- Information is scattered across many apps (Notion, Google Docs, Figma, Linear, etc.)
- Losing track of important pages you forgot to bookmark
- Context switching between too many browser tabs
- No unified way to search across all your work tools
- Repeatedly searching for the same pages you visit often

## How it works

Press ⌘J (Mac) or Ctrl+J (Windows/Linux) to open a command palette overlay. Start typing to instantly search everything you've visited. Results appear in milliseconds, ranked by relevance and recency.

## Core features

### Instant search
Search your browsing history across 100+ work applications. Finds pages by title, URL, or content. Results load instantly from local index.

### AI-powered answers
Ask natural language questions and get answers based on your work context. Example: "What were the action items from the Q3 planning doc?"

### Floating notes
Persistent notes window that stays on top of other windows. Quick capture for ideas, todos, meeting notes. Accessible from anywhere with a keyboard shortcut.

### Pins
Save frequently accessed pages for one-click access. Like bookmarks but faster and integrated into the command palette.

### Quick actions (slash commands)
Create new documents instantly without leaving your current page:
- /doc - New Google Doc
- /sheet - New Google Sheet
- /slide - New Google Slides
- /figma - New Figma file
- /notion - New Notion page
- /linear - New Linear issue
- /notes - Open floating notes
- /pins - View pinned pages

### Keyboard-first design
Entire interface navigable by keyboard. Up/down arrows to navigate, Enter to open, Escape to close. No mouse required.

## Supported applications

Daysift indexes pages from productivity and work applications including:

**Documents & wikis**: Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides, Notion, Confluence, Coda, Dropbox Paper, Quip

**Design**: Figma, Canva, Miro, FigJam, Whimsical

**Development**: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Linear, Jira, Vercel, Netlify, AWS Console

**Communication**: Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar, Zoom, Microsoft Teams

**Project management**: Asana, Monday.com, Trello, Basecamp, ClickUp, Todoist

**Other**: Airtable, HubSpot, Salesforce, Intercom, Zendesk, and 100+ more

The extension uses an allowlist approach - it only indexes recognized work applications, not general browsing or personal sites.

## Privacy and security

Daysift is designed with privacy as a core principle:

- **Local-first**: All data is stored on your device in the browser's local storage. No cloud servers store your browsing data.
- **No account required**: Works immediately after install. No signup, no login, no email required for core features.
- **No tracking**: No analytics on your browsing behavior or search queries.
- **Allowlist-only**: Only indexes known work applications, not your entire browsing history.
- **AI is optional**: AI features require explicit opt-in consent. When used, only page titles and URLs are sent (not page content).
- **Data stays local**: Uninstalling the extension deletes all stored data.

## Who it's for

- **Knowledge workers** who use multiple browser-based tools daily
- **Developers** managing code, issues, docs, and deployments across many platforms
- **Designers** working across Figma, documentation, and project management tools
- **Product managers** juggling specs, roadmaps, analytics, and communication tools
- **Researchers** collecting information across many sources
- **Remote workers** whose entire workflow lives in the browser
- **Anyone** who has ever thought "where did I see that page?"

## Use cases

- Find a Google Doc you were editing last week
- Locate a Figma file a colleague shared in Slack
- Search for a GitHub PR you reviewed recently
- Recall what Notion pages you visited for a specific project
- Quickly access your most-used dashboards without bookmarking
- Take quick notes during a meeting without leaving your current tab
- Create a new Google Sheet without navigating to Google Drive first

## Comparison to other tools

- **Chrome history**: Daysift is faster, searches more fields, and has better ranking
- **Bookmarks**: Daysift is dynamic (no manual saving) and includes search
- **Tab managers**: Daysift searches history, not just open tabs
- **Spotlight/Alfred/Raycast**: Daysift is specifically for browser content and works inside Chrome
- **Full-text search tools**: Daysift is lighter weight and privacy-focused (no content indexing)

## Pricing

- **Free**: Full history search (12 results), 30 AI queries/month, 5 notes, 5 pins
- **Pro** ($4/month): More search results, 100 AI queries/month, unlimited notes and pins
- **Pro+** ($8/month): Everything unlimited including AI queries

Free tier has no time limit - use it indefinitely.

## Technical details

- Chrome extension (Manifest V3)
- Works in Chrome, Brave, Arc, Edge, and Chromium-based browsers
- Lightweight: minimal CPU and memory usage
- Offline capable: search works without internet connection
- Fast: local IndexedDB storage, sub-100ms search results
